newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros army downs French flag to jeers of islanders.
newsitem.headline: Comoros army downs French flag to jeers of islanders.

text.p: Troops armed with machineguns and hand grenades were booed and jeered by islanders when they brought down a French flag on the Comoros island of Anjouan on Saturday, witnesses reported.
The flag, a symbol of the growing secessionist movement on Anjouan, had been hoisted during the night on an electricity pole at a football stadium.
It was the third time in a week that the French flag -- which flew in the Comoros until independence in 1975 -- had been raised on Anjouan.
On Wednesday the authorities released two leaders of the Anjouan secessionist movement after they were briefly detained.
Anjouan residents told reporters many islanders were planning to boycott the Comoros Day celebrations on July 6, marking the anniversary of the Comoros declaration of independence.

The archipelego, with a population of 190,000, became independent from France in 1975 but some islanders appear to want to return to the French fold, saying life in the Comoros is reduced by poverty, corruption and succession of coups.

The secessionist movement has gained momentum from a serious economic crisis, with civil servants frequently complaining of non-payment of their salaries and political unrest. Several people were killed in clashes between the army and islanders on Anjouan in March.
